text.p: German metals and trading group Metallgesellschaft AG is expected to post "clearly" higher profits in its 1995/1996 business year, management board chairman Kajo Neukirchen said on Friday.
Neukirchen however declined to make more specific comments.
Neukirchen told a group of journalists that sales at the end of September stood at 15 billion marks compared with 17.6 billion marks a year earlier.
The group had also managed to pare back its bank debts to 700 million marks in the 1995/1996 business year compared with 1.5 billion marks a year earlier.
Liquidity dropped to 1.4 billion marks from 2.2 billion marks.
Neukirchen also said the group continued to reduce its risk, several years after being saved from the brink of bankruptcy by creditor banks.

While 57 percent of the group's turnover was considered to be in the highest risk category in 1993/1994, that percentage dropped to 44 percent in 1994/1995 and is slated to sink to 28 percent in 1997/1998, Neukirchen said.
He said the group's industrial activities rose to 60 percent of the entire business activities from 39 percent while trading activity shrank to 40 percent from 61 percent.
Neukirchen said the group's goal was to have a 70-30 distribution between the two areas in favour of the industrial side.
